tools.name: create_form
tools.description: Create a form in the team this token is bound to. Pass the questions array and report configuration in one call instead of following up with per-question calls. In the outcome_quiz scene report.outcomes is REQUIRED at create time (TrueFalse votes via trueOutcomes/falseOutcomes). In the ai_quiz scene nothing is scored: set custom question codes and pass report.aiReport.instructions referencing them as {{code}} in this same call. For a scored_quiz with dimensions, define report.dimensionAnalysis.dimensions with codes and formulas over question codes in this same call; a question may override its score for one dimension via choices[i].dimensionScores (TrueFalse: trueDimensionScores/falseDimensionScores). The returned structuredContent.fields carries each question code — read those first if you need to reference them: a scored_quiz totals its question scores by default, and only needs report.formula (e.g. {{q_a}} * 2 + {{q_b}}) for a custom total; dimensions go in report.dimensionAnalysis via update_form / set_dimension_analysis. Creates the primary language only; add other languages with create_form_translation. Limit: a quiz holds at most 50 questions on every plan (page breaks, statements and carousels do not count). An ai_quiz holds at most 20. Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

title.description: Form title (1-200 characters). Plain text: no HTML or Markdown.

scene.description: knowledge_quiz = graded exam (correctAnswer + score); scored_quiz = option scoring + report formula; outcome_quiz = typing quiz (votes decide which outcome type wins); ai_quiz = no scoring, an AI writes each report from report.aiReport (may include Attachment uploads). Immutable after creation.

description.description:
Optional form description. Allows description-scope rich text (including ). Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

questions.description: Optional. A list of questions/page breaks to create at once, written into form.fields in order. Question types: SingleCheck/MultiCheck/TrueFalse; FillBlank (free text — scored in quiz via correctAnswer, an unscored data-collection field in scored_quiz); DropDown (single or multiple via `multiple`, use it instead of SingleCheck/MultiCheck when there are more than 20 choices); Ordering (quiz only, correctAnswer = all choices in the correct order); NumberField (quiz: optional numeric correctAnswer + score; scored_quiz: the submitted number feeds report formulas); Rate (scored_quiz / ai_quiz; in scored_quiz the 1..steps rating value is the question score unless per-star scores are set in the web app); Attachment (ai_quiz only: a file upload with `kind` image / audio / video / document that the AI reads). Insert a page break with { type: "Breaker" }, which the AI can interleave between questions to paginate. Display blocks collect no answer: { type: "Statement", content } is a rich-text passage (intro / section lead-in / disclaimer) and { type: "Swiper", items } an image carousel. At most 100 items.

items.description: One question, a page break, or a display block (Statement / Swiper). FIELD APPLICABILITY — `type` is the only field the schema always requires; `type` (plus the form scene) decides which of the remaining fields apply, and one that does not apply is either rejected with an explanatory error or ignored, so never pass it. Breaker (page break) takes nothing but `type`. Display blocks collect no answer, are never scored and are allowed in every scene: Statement takes `content` (the rich text IS the block) and Swiper takes `items` (an image carousel); both also accept an optional `name`, a label used by the web editor only, and neither takes any question field. Every question type takes `name` (required) plus the optional `code` / `description` / `explain` / `required`. Type-specific fields: SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering need `choices` (DropDown also takes `multiple`; Ordering also takes `shuffle`); TrueFalse has a fixed pair of options and takes `trueLabel` / `falseLabel` instead of `choices`; NumberField takes `min` / `max` / `unit` / `decimalPlaces`; Rate takes `steps` / `words` / `rateStyle`; Attachment takes `kind` (required) / `maxFiles`. Scene rules for scoring: quiz — `correctAnswer` plus `score` > 0 are REQUIRED on SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering, optional on FillBlank (add `aiMatch` to have AI grade it instead of exact string match) and NumberField (omit both and the question is just a data-collection field); scored_quiz — score each option via choices[i].score; `correctAnswer` / `score` are rejected on NumberField and Rate (the submitted value is the score) and on FillBlank (free text is collected only, never scored); outcome — nothing is scored: `correctAnswer` / `score` / `aiMatch` are all rejected, every choice needs `outcomes` (TrueFalse votes via `trueOutcomes` / `falseOutcomes`); ai_quiz — nothing is scored: `correctAnswer` / `score` / `aiMatch` / choices[i].score are all rejected; an AI reads the answers and writes the report from report.aiReport. Type availability per scene: Ordering is knowledge_quiz-only; FillBlank works in knowledge_quiz (optionally scored) and in scored_quiz (data-collection only — its answer never feeds a score or a report formula); Rate works in scored_quiz and ai_quiz only; the outcome_quiz scene accepts only SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / TrueFalse / Breaker; the ai_quiz scene accepts every type except Ordering, plus Attachment (ai_quiz-only via MCP, at most 2 per form).

type.description: Question type; Breaker means a page break (the frontend pushes subsequent questions to the next page), no name/choices etc. needed; Statement / Swiper are display-only blocks that collect no answer

code.description: Optional stable identifier for this question (field code). Omit it to let the server auto-generate one. Set a meaningful code (e.g. "q1") when report.formula or a dimension needs to reference this question, so you can write the formula as `{{q1}}` in the same call instead of round-tripping via get_form. Rules: start with a letter or underscore, then only letters/digits/underscores (no hyphens, spaces, or leading digit), at most 64 chars, and not a reserved math word (e, E, pi, PI, tau, phi, i, Infinity, NaN, true, false, null, undefined). Must be unique among all items in the form.

name.description:
Question stem text. Allows plain text or restricted HTML (tag allowlist:

/ /

description.description:
Optional supplementary note for the question. Allows a wider HTML subset: everything the stem allows +

Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

explain.description:
Optional answer explanation. The frontend renders it in the question's "answer explanation" field (DescriptionEditor); the rich-text rules are identical to description. Do not stuff the answer explanation into description — that is the question's supplementary note and will not be shown as an explanation to respondents/graders. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,

required.description: Whether the question is required, default false

min.description: NumberField only: minimum allowed input value (respondents cannot submit a smaller number). Rejected for other question types.

max.description: NumberField only: maximum allowed input value (must be >= min). Rejected for other question types.

unit.description: NumberField only: display unit suffix shown after the input, e.g. "kg" / "$" / "min". Rejected for other question types.

decimalPlaces.description: NumberField only: how many decimal places respondents may enter (stored as the field's numeric precision), default 0 = integers only. Rejected for other question types.

steps.description: Rate only: number of rating steps, i.e. the highest rating (3-10, default 5). In the scored_quiz scene the submitted rating value (1..steps) is the question score, unless a per-star score is configured in the web app. Rejected for other question types.

words.description: Rate only: optional scale labels evenly distributed under the rating control, e.g. ["Poor", "Excellent"] for the two endpoints (up to 5 labels). Rejected for other question types.

rateStyle.description: Rate only: how the rating control looks — "star" (default, a row of stars) or "number" (a row of numbered circles 1..steps, reads more like a professional self-assessment scale). Display only: the submitted value is 1..steps either way. Rejected for other question types.

choices.description: Choice-based questions only (SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering), where it is required; ignored for every other type, including TrueFalse — its two options come from trueLabel / falseLabel. Per-type limits: SingleCheck / MultiCheck 2-100 items — for a longer list use DropDown (2-300 items) instead; Ordering 2-10 items. IMPORTANT (knowledge_quiz scene): vary the position of the correct option(s) across questions — do NOT always place the correct answer first. Distribute correct answers roughly evenly over all positions so they are not predictable.

code.description: Optional stable identifier for this choice (option code). Omit to auto-generate. Same identifier rules as the question code; must be unique among the choices of this question. correctAnswer may reference a choice by its label or its code.

score.description: Used only in the scored_quiz scene; the score added when this choice is selected (generates partialScoring). Ignored in the knowledge_quiz scene; rejected in the outcome_quiz scene.

code.description: Outcome code from report.outcomes

weight.description: Votes this pick casts for the outcome; omit for 1. Decimals allowed, 0 = counts for nothing.

outcomes.description: Outcome scene only, and required there on every choice: the outcomes this choice votes for when selected (each code must exist in report.outcomes; a choice may vote for multiple outcomes). Use [] for a neutral choice that votes for nothing. Rejected in the knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz scenes. Each item is an outcome code (one vote) or { code, weight } to make this pick count more or less — e.g. { "code": "lion", "weight": 2 } for a question that should decide the result more than the others. The outcome with the most total votes wins.

dimensionScores.description: scored_quiz scene only: the points this choice adds to each dimension when selected, as a map of dimension code → score, e.g. { "dim_d": 3, "dim_i": 1 }. Each entry overrides this choice's score for that one dimension; a dimension not listed falls back to the plain choice `score`, and an explicit 0 really counts 0. Dimension scores still come only from each dimension's required formula: inside it `{{q}}` is the sum of the selected choices' override-or-score for that dimension, and a question the formula does not reference adds nothing. Codes must exist in report.dimensionAnalysis.dimensions — give dimensions[].code and reference them in the same create_form call. `score` remains the overall score (summed by default, or fed to report.formula when set). Rejected in the knowledge_quiz / outcome_quiz scenes.

multiple.description: DropDown only: allow selecting multiple options (default false = single select). Affects the quiz-scene correctAnswer shape: an array of labels/codes when true, a single one when false. Rejected for other question types (SingleCheck/MultiCheck are inherently single/multi).

shuffle.description: Ordering only: shuffle the displayed choice order for each respondent. Defaults to true for MCP-created questions — the stored choices order would otherwise leak the correct order when correctAnswer matches it. Pass false only when the initial order is intentionally meaningful. Rejected for other question types.

code.description: Outcome code from report.outcomes

weight.description: Votes this pick casts for the outcome; omit for 1. Decimals allowed, 0 = counts for nothing.

trueOutcomes.description: Outcome scene + TrueFalse only (required there together with falseOutcomes): the outcomes that answering "true" votes for. Use [] for a side that votes for nothing. Rejected for other question types / scenes. Each item is an outcome code (one vote) or { code, weight } to make this pick count more or less — e.g. { "code": "lion", "weight": 2 } for a question that should decide the result more than the others. The outcome with the most total votes wins.

code.description: Outcome code from report.outcomes

weight.description: Votes this pick casts for the outcome; omit for 1. Decimals allowed, 0 = counts for nothing.

falseOutcomes.description: Outcome scene + TrueFalse only (required there together with trueOutcomes): the outcomes that answering "false" votes for. Use [] for a side that votes for nothing. Rejected for other question types / scenes. Each item is an outcome code (one vote) or { code, weight } to make this pick count more or less — e.g. { "code": "lion", "weight": 2 } for a question that should decide the result more than the others. The outcome with the most total votes wins.

trueDimensionScores.description: scored_quiz scene + TrueFalse only: the points answering "true" adds to each dimension, as a map of dimension code → score (same semantics as choices[i].dimensionScores). Rejected for other question types / scenes.

falseDimensionScores.description: scored_quiz scene + TrueFalse only: the points answering "false" adds to each dimension, as a map of dimension code → score (same semantics as choices[i].dimensionScores). Rejected for other question types / scenes.

trueLabel.description: TrueFalse only: custom display text for the "true" option (e.g. "Yes" / "Agree"). Ignored for other question types. Leave empty to fall back to the built-in default for the form language ("Correct" in English forms). Does not change the stored answer value, which stays "true".

falseLabel.description: TrueFalse only: custom display text for the "false" option (e.g. "No" / "Disagree"). Ignored for other question types. Leave empty to fall back to the built-in default for the form language ("Incorrect" in English forms). Does not change the stored answer value, which stays "false".

kind.description: Attachment only, and required there: what respondents upload, which also decides how the AI reads it (image = vision, audio / video = transcribed, document = text extracted). Per-file limits: image ≤10MB; audio ≤10MB and ≤180s; video ≤20MB and ≤60s; document ≤10MB. Fixed once the question exists — to change it, delete_question and add a new one. Rejected for other question types.

maxFiles.description: Attachment only: how many files a respondent may upload to this question (1-3, default 3). Rejected for other question types.

content.description:
Statement only, and required there: the text respondents read — an intro, a section lead-in, instructions, a disclaimer. The block renders this and nothing else. Same rich-text rules as `description` (headings / lists / links / / math formulas). Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

image.description: The slide image: a media ID returned by finalize_image_upload, or the media URL of an image already in this team library. Required — the answer page renders the images and nothing else.

title.description: Optional slide label. Shown in the web editor only (the answer page renders the image), and translatable per language.

description.description: Optional slide note. Web editor only, same as title.

items.description: Swiper only, and required there: the carousel slides in display order, 1-10 of them. Upload the images with prepare_image_upload / finalize_image_upload first and pass the returned media IDs. Rejected for every other type.

anyOf.description: SingleCheck / single-select DropDown: one choice label or code. FillBlank: the standard answer text.
MultiCheck / multi-select DropDown (multiple=true): the label or code of every correct choice. Ordering: ALL choice labels/codes in the correct order (order-sensitive).
NumberField: a finite number, matched exactly.

correctAnswer.description: The "correct answer" of the knowledge_quiz scene; setting it makes the question scored, so pair it with a positive `score`. The shape follows the question type — see the anyOf branches; a choice is referenced by its label or its code, so reference it by code whenever the same label appears more than once (Ordering rejects an ambiguous label outright). Required on SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering in the knowledge_quiz scene, optional on FillBlank / NumberField there. NumberField answers must be typeable within min / max and decimalPlaces. Rejected for Rate (a rating field), rejected for FillBlank in the scored_quiz scene (free text is collected only there), and rejected in the outcome_quiz scene (no right or wrong answers there). In the scored_quiz scene prefer choices[i].score per option; passing correctAnswer + score there only falls back to "the matching choice gets score, others get 0".

score.description: Points this question is worth, default 0 (not scored). Quiz scene: awarded when the answer matches correctAnswer, and a positive value is required once correctAnswer is set. Scored Quiz scene: pairing it with correctAnswer enables the fallback mode above, but choices[i].score is more flexible. Rejected in the outcome_quiz scene, for Rate, and — in the scored_quiz scene — for NumberField (where the submitted number itself is the score) and FillBlank (collected only, never scored).

aiMatch.description: Only for FillBlank in the knowledge_quiz scene. Enables AI grading: the AI compares the respondent answer against correctAnswer and scores by accuracy, instead of requiring an exact string match. Requires correctAnswer (the standard answer) and score > 0 (the score earned when accuracy reaches the threshold). Pass an empty object {} to enable with default settings; omit for plain exact-match grading.

accuracy.description: Accuracy threshold (0-100) at or above which the full score is awarded. Default 80.

extraLevels.description: Optional partial-credit tiers for answers below the full-score threshold. Each {accuracy, score}: if the AI accuracy is below the threshold but >= this tier accuracy, this score is awarded. Tiers are matched from highest accuracy to lowest; if none match, the score is 0.

report.description: Report configuration. knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz: overallAnalysis fields are flat at the top level and dimensionAnalysis is nested (strongly recommended for the scored_quiz scene, rejected in the knowledge_quiz scene, which has no dimensions). outcome: only the outcomes key (required at create time) and sectionOrder are allowed. ai_quiz: only aiReport and sectionOrder are allowed.

title.description: Overall analysis title, default "Overall Scored Quiz Analysis"

formula.description: Optional custom total-score formula for the scored_quiz scene. Leave it out to use the default: the overall score is the sum of every scored question (choice scores, plus the star value / configured score of Rate questions; NumberField raw values are not summed) and the full mark is the sum of each question's highest attainable score. Set it only when you need weights, dimension combinations or NumberField values. In update_form, omitting it keeps the current formula; pass "" to remove it. Question codes must be wrapped in `{{code}}` (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}` for custom question codes, or `{{__field_abc}} + {{__field_def}}` for auto-generated ones); bare codes are rejected. It may also reference dimension codes the same way (e.g. `{{dim_d}} * 2 + {{dim_i}}`): dimensions are computed first, so the overall score can be a weighted sum of dimension scores; a dimension referenced here cannot be removed later. Supported operators: + - * / ( ); every referenced code must exist in the current form (questions and dimensions). Setting dimension formulas does NOT cover this — the overall formula is separate.

summaryTemplate.description:
Summary template. Allows description-scope rich text (headings/lists/links/images/ etc.). Supports math formulas: write `` with the LaTeX in data-latex and nothing inside; the server renders it. Two variables are available: write {{score}} (the overall score) and {{level}} (the matched level label); they are stored as ``. Any other variable is rejected. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

levels.description: Score levels (at most 20), ordered by upper bound ascending. Example: [{label:"Needs improvement",upTo:60},{label:"Good",upTo:80},{label:"Excellent"}] means (-∞,60) / [60,80) / [80,+∞). The last level must omit upTo. In the scored_quiz scene these levels are matched against the overall score: report.formula when set, otherwise the sum of every scored question.

upTo.description: Upper bound (exclusive); omit for the last level

description.description:
Result-page text shown when the score falls in this level. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading".

cta.description: Optional CTA button shown on the result page when the score falls in this level (e.g. "Book a consultation" for the low band). Providing it enables the button. Overall levels only — dimension levels reject it.

newWindow.description: Deprecated and ignored: the CTA link always opens in a new window.

redirectUrl.description: http(s) link respondents are sent to right after submitting when the score falls in this level, instead of seeing the result page. Only takes effect while redirects are switched on (update_form_settings resultRedirect, Pro). In update_form, omit it to keep the link of the current level with the same label; pass "" or null to remove it. Overall levels only.

dimensionAnalysis.description: Multi-dimension analysis (radar chart + per-dimension breakdown); scored_quiz scene only — knowledge quizzes have no dimensions and reject it. Each dimension has a stable code (pass dimensions[].code or let the server generate one; returned in structuredContent). Every dimension needs a formula over question codes (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}`); a question may override its score for one dimension via choices[i].dimensionScores, otherwise the formula uses its plain choice score. If you set custom question codes you can configure everything in one create_form call; otherwise create the questions first, then get_form to read the auto-generated codes.

title.description: Multi-dimension analysis title

showRadarChart.description: Whether to show the radar chart, default true

showStandardLine.description: Whether to show the standard-score line on the radar chart

dimensions.description: The dimension list (at most 50). Pass an empty array (or omit) to mean "no dimensions".

code.description: Optional stable identifier for the dimension (same rules as question codes: starts with a letter or underscore, letters/digits/underscores only). Set it when questions reference the dimension via choices[i].dimensionScores in the same create_form call. When updating, pass the existing code to keep it; if omitted, a dimension with the same name keeps its current code, otherwise one is generated.

standardScore.description: Standard score: the radar-chart standard line and the dimension full mark. When omitted it defaults to the attainable maximum: the formula evaluated with every referenced question at its highest score for this dimension (choices[i].dimensionScores override, else the choice score); 0 when that cannot be estimated, e.g. the formula uses NumberField / date questions.

formula.description: Required: the dimension score formula, usually the sum of the questions in this dimension. Question codes must be wrapped in `{{code}}` (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}` when you set custom question codes, or `{{__field_abc}} + {{__field_def}}` for auto-generated ones); bare codes are rejected. Inside a dimension formula `{{q}}` is the question's score for THIS dimension: its choices[i].dimensionScores override when set, otherwise the plain choice score. A dimension formula cannot reference other dimensions (only report.formula can). Supported operators: + - * / ( ).

weight.description: Weight (used when computing weighted overall score), default 1

description.description: Dimension description (plain text)

levels.description: Optional dimension levels (at most 20), ordered by upper bound ascending. Example: [{label:"Weak",upTo:60},{label:"Strong"}]. The last level must omit upTo.

upTo.description: Upper bound (exclusive); omit for the last level

outcomes.description: outcome_quiz: the outcome types this quiz can result in (required at create time, 1-50 items). Each question choice votes for outcome codes; the outcome with the most votes wins (ties resolved by array order, earlier wins). ai_quiz: optional result tags (0-10; [] removes them) — before writing each report the AI picks one tag per respondent, so leads can be filtered and pushed by it; put the criteria for choosing a tag in its description, and an optional cta shown under that respondent's report. Tags are internal: respondents never see the tag name. Rejected in the knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz scenes.

code.description: Unique outcome code you choose (e.g. "lion"); choices reference it in their outcomes votes. Treat it as a stable identifier — renaming it later breaks references from questions.

name.description: Outcome display name shown on the result page, e.g. "Lion — The Decisive Leader". Plain text.

description.description:
Result-page content shown when this outcome wins. Allows description-scope rich text (headings/lists/links/images etc.). Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

cta.description: Optional CTA button shown on the result page when this outcome wins (e.g. "Book a consultation"). Providing it enables the button.

newWindow.description: Deprecated and ignored: the CTA link always opens in a new window.

redirectUrl.description: outcome_quiz only: http(s) link respondents are sent to right after submitting when this outcome wins, instead of seeing the result page. Only takes effect while redirects are switched on (update_form_settings resultRedirect, Pro). In update_form, omit it to keep the outcome's current link; pass "" or null to remove it. Rejected on ai_quiz result tags.

aiReport.description: ai_quiz scene only (rejected elsewhere): how the AI writes each respondent's report. Sub-keys are merged — pass only the one you change; null or "" clears it.

instructions.description: Generation instructions: what the report should cover, how to read the answers, what to recommend. Plain text (one paragraph per line) or description-scope rich text HTML. Reference a question as {{code}} (visible input questions only; call get_form for the codes) — the AI is pointed at that answer, the answer text itself is not inlined. Unknown codes are rejected. At most 20000 visible characters. get_form returns it in this same {{code}} form.

style.description: Optional style and rules (tone, length, things to avoid), plain text, at most 5000 characters.

length.description: Report length: brief (about 150 words, verdict + 1-2 findings + next steps), standard (default, about 300 words, 2-4 sections, one chart) or detailed (about 650 words, up to 6 sections and 3 charts). null restores standard. brief and standard are hard caps: a longer word count, more sections or more detail asked for in instructions or style is ignored. Only detailed lets a length rule written in style take precedence.

sectionOrder.description: Any scene: the order of the movable result-page sections — dimension (dimension breakdown / radar), booking (the Cal.com booking block), feedback (the feedback block). The overall score / outcome always stays on top and the answer review / share area at the bottom. Keys you leave out keep their default relative order after the ones you list; [] restores the default (booking, dimension, feedback).

levelOrder.description: knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz only: display order of the score levels — asc (default, lowest level first) or desc (highest level first). Applies to the overall levels and every dimension's levels, in the editor and on the result page's level scale. Display only: levels are still stored and matched by minScore ascending, so pass report.levels in ascending order either way. null restores asc.

scoreStyle.description: knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz only: how the result page's overall score card shows the result — scale (a level bar with a marker), ring (a progress ring with the score inside), gauge (a semicircle gauge split by level with a needle) or steps (one bar per level, taller for higher levels). Display only. null (the default) follows the personalized theme: the applied library design's style, or scale when none is applied. Styles that need data the quiz lacks (e.g. steps without levels) fall back to scale.

systemText.description: Optional. Answer-page system text overrides as a key→text map; empty values are dropped and fall back to the language default.

theme.description: Optional visual theme matching the quiz topic/mood. Default light. Pick the one that best fits the quiz: light (clean neutral bright; default — formal/general quizzes); corporate (professional blue+gray; B2B, career, business assessments); dark (modern sleek dark; tech, night, cool personality quizzes); cupcake (soft pink cute rounded; fun, food, kids, lighthearted); pastel (gentle pastel artsy; lifestyle, aesthetics, soft mood); valentine (pink romantic hearts; love, relationships, holidays); synthwave (neon purple/pink retro; gaming, trends, bold personality); luxury (dark + gold premium; finance, luxury brands, high-end); forest (deep green nature; environment, health, outdoors); coffee (warm brown cozy; food & drink, cafe, lifestyle); autumn (warm orange/brown seasonal; autumn, cozy, harvest); halloween (purple+orange spooky; Halloween, horror, festive fun); night (deep calm blue; astronomy, mindfulness, calm tech); cyberpunk (high-contrast neon yellow; tech, esports, gaming).

openGraph.description: Social share card (Open Graph) settings: the title / description / image shown when the answer link is shared to social media or chat apps. In update_form each sub-key is merged independently (only the keys you pass change; pass an empty string to clear one). SEO keywords are generated automatically and cannot be set here.

title.description: Share card title (at most 50 characters). Plain text. Empty string clears it (falls back to the form title).

description.description: Share card description (at most 100 characters). Plain text. Empty string clears it.

image.description: Share card image: a media ID returned by finalize_image_upload, or a media URL. Recommended 1200x630 for good social previews. Empty string clears it.

tools.name: get_form
tools.description: View one form of the current team in full, including the questions list fields[] and the report configuration. For outcome forms, the outcome codes that question votes reference live in report.outcomeAnalysis.outcomes. `language` is the primary language; existing non-primary language versions are listed in `translationLanguages`.

includeFields.description: Whether to return fields[] (raw data of questions + page breaks), default true. For large forms you can pass false to skip

includeReport.description: Whether to return the report configuration, default true

tools.name: list_forms
tools.description: List the forms of the current team. Returned in reverse chronological order of creation, without question content (use get_form for details).

tools.name: update_form
tools.description: Update a form of the current team: title / description / isActive / flagImg / landingImage / theme / report / openGraph / language / systemText. flagImg is the quiz cover, landingImage the landing-page cover (sets the image only, does not toggle the landing page); both take a media id from finalize_image_upload, a media URL, or "" to clear. report and openGraph (the social share card on the answer link) merge by sub-key — only what you pass is replaced, "" clears an openGraph sub-key; in the outcome_quiz scene outcomes are matched by code so existing images survive, and removing an outcome still referenced by question votes is rejected. systemText is replaced wholesale ({} clears it). language is changeable only while the form has no language versions; scene never. Questions go through add_question / update_question / delete_question / move_question, dimensionAnalysis alone through set_dimension_analysis.

title.description: New title

description.description:
New description; pass an empty string to clear. Allows description-scope rich text (including ). Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

flagImg.description: Quiz cover image: a media ID returned by finalize_image_upload, or a media URL. Pass an empty string to clear the cover.

landingImage.description: Landing page cover image: a media ID returned by finalize_image_upload, or a media URL. Pass an empty string to clear it. Note: this only sets the image and does NOT toggle the landing page on/off; the landing image is shown only when the landing page is enabled.

theme.description: New visual theme for the answer page. Only this sub-key of personalized is changed; settings are kept. Optional visual theme matching the quiz topic/mood. Default light. Pick the one that best fits the quiz: light (clean neutral bright; default — formal/general quizzes); corporate (professional blue+gray; B2B, career, business assessments); dark (modern sleek dark; tech, night, cool personality quizzes); cupcake (soft pink cute rounded; fun, food, kids, lighthearted); pastel (gentle pastel artsy; lifestyle, aesthetics, soft mood); valentine (pink romantic hearts; love, relationships, holidays); synthwave (neon purple/pink retro; gaming, trends, bold personality); luxury (dark + gold premium; finance, luxury brands, high-end); forest (deep green nature; environment, health, outdoors); coffee (warm brown cozy; food & drink, cafe, lifestyle); autumn (warm orange/brown seasonal; autumn, cozy, harvest); halloween (purple+orange spooky; Halloween, horror, festive fun); night (deep calm blue; astronomy, mindfulness, calm tech); cyberpunk (high-contrast neon yellow; tech, esports, gaming).

openGraph.description: Social share card (Open Graph) settings: the title / description / image shown when the answer link is shared to social media or chat apps. In update_form each sub-key is merged independently (only the keys you pass change; pass an empty string to clear one). SEO keywords are generated automatically and cannot be set here.

title.description: Share card title (at most 50 characters). Plain text. Empty string clears it (falls back to the form title).

description.description: Share card description (at most 100 characters). Plain text. Empty string clears it.

image.description: Share card image: a media ID returned by finalize_image_upload, or a media URL. Recommended 1200x630 for good social previews. Empty string clears it.

report.description: Report configuration, merged by sub-key into form.report: passing overallAnalysis fields (title/formula/levels/summaryTemplate) replaces overallAnalysis, except that an omitted formula keeps the current one (pass formula: "" to remove it and fall back to the default sum); passing dimensionAnalysis replaces the dimension list (scored_quiz only; codes are kept by code or by name, omitted title / radar settings are preserved; an empty dimensions array clears it; a dimension still referenced by a question's dimensionScores or by report.formula cannot be removed); in the outcome_quiz scene passing outcomes replaces the outcome list (matched by code, existing images kept; cannot be emptied, and removing an outcome still referenced by question votes is rejected); passing sectionOrder replaces the result-page section order ([] restores the default); passing levelOrder sets the level display order (asc / desc, knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz only); passing scoreStyle sets the score card style (scale / ring / gauge / steps, null follows the theme; knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz only); unspecified parts are kept. Common usage: either set custom question codes in create_form and pass report.formula / dimensionAnalysis in the same call, or call create_form first to get the auto-generated field codes, then update_form to fill in report.formula and/or dimensionAnalysis (which reference question codes).

title.description: Overall analysis title, default "Overall Scored Quiz Analysis"

formula.description: Optional custom total-score formula for the scored_quiz scene. Leave it out to use the default: the overall score is the sum of every scored question (choice scores, plus the star value / configured score of Rate questions; NumberField raw values are not summed) and the full mark is the sum of each question's highest attainable score. Set it only when you need weights, dimension combinations or NumberField values. In update_form, omitting it keeps the current formula; pass "" to remove it. Question codes must be wrapped in `{{code}}` (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}` for custom question codes, or `{{__field_abc}} + {{__field_def}}` for auto-generated ones); bare codes are rejected. It may also reference dimension codes the same way (e.g. `{{dim_d}} * 2 + {{dim_i}}`): dimensions are computed first, so the overall score can be a weighted sum of dimension scores; a dimension referenced here cannot be removed later. Supported operators: + - * / ( ); every referenced code must exist in the current form (questions and dimensions). Setting dimension formulas does NOT cover this — the overall formula is separate.

summaryTemplate.description:
Summary template. Allows description-scope rich text (headings/lists/links/images/ etc.). Supports math formulas: write `` with the LaTeX in data-latex and nothing inside; the server renders it. Two variables are available: write {{score}} (the overall score) and {{level}} (the matched level label); they are stored as ``. Any other variable is rejected. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

levels.description: Score levels (at most 20), ordered by upper bound ascending. Example: [{label:"Needs improvement",upTo:60},{label:"Good",upTo:80},{label:"Excellent"}] means (-∞,60) / [60,80) / [80,+∞). The last level must omit upTo. In the scored_quiz scene these levels are matched against the overall score: report.formula when set, otherwise the sum of every scored question.

upTo.description: Upper bound (exclusive); omit for the last level

description.description:
Result-page text shown when the score falls in this level. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading".

cta.description: Optional CTA button shown on the result page when the score falls in this level (e.g. "Book a consultation" for the low band). Providing it enables the button. Overall levels only — dimension levels reject it.

newWindow.description: Deprecated and ignored: the CTA link always opens in a new window.

redirectUrl.description: http(s) link respondents are sent to right after submitting when the score falls in this level, instead of seeing the result page. Only takes effect while redirects are switched on (update_form_settings resultRedirect, Pro). In update_form, omit it to keep the link of the current level with the same label; pass "" or null to remove it. Overall levels only.

dimensionAnalysis.description: Multi-dimension analysis (radar chart + per-dimension breakdown); scored_quiz scene only — knowledge quizzes have no dimensions and reject it. Each dimension has a stable code (pass dimensions[].code or let the server generate one; returned in structuredContent). Every dimension needs a formula over question codes (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}`); a question may override its score for one dimension via choices[i].dimensionScores, otherwise the formula uses its plain choice score. If you set custom question codes you can configure everything in one create_form call; otherwise create the questions first, then get_form to read the auto-generated codes.

title.description: Multi-dimension analysis title

showRadarChart.description: Whether to show the radar chart, default true

showStandardLine.description: Whether to show the standard-score line on the radar chart

dimensions.description: The dimension list (at most 50). Pass an empty array (or omit) to mean "no dimensions".

code.description: Optional stable identifier for the dimension (same rules as question codes: starts with a letter or underscore, letters/digits/underscores only). Set it when questions reference the dimension via choices[i].dimensionScores in the same create_form call. When updating, pass the existing code to keep it; if omitted, a dimension with the same name keeps its current code, otherwise one is generated.

standardScore.description: Standard score: the radar-chart standard line and the dimension full mark. When omitted it defaults to the attainable maximum: the formula evaluated with every referenced question at its highest score for this dimension (choices[i].dimensionScores override, else the choice score); 0 when that cannot be estimated, e.g. the formula uses NumberField / date questions.

formula.description: Required: the dimension score formula, usually the sum of the questions in this dimension. Question codes must be wrapped in `{{code}}` (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}` when you set custom question codes, or `{{__field_abc}} + {{__field_def}}` for auto-generated ones); bare codes are rejected. Inside a dimension formula `{{q}}` is the question's score for THIS dimension: its choices[i].dimensionScores override when set, otherwise the plain choice score. A dimension formula cannot reference other dimensions (only report.formula can). Supported operators: + - * / ( ).

weight.description: Weight (used when computing weighted overall score), default 1

description.description: Dimension description (plain text)

levels.description: Optional dimension levels (at most 20), ordered by upper bound ascending. Example: [{label:"Weak",upTo:60},{label:"Strong"}]. The last level must omit upTo.

upTo.description: Upper bound (exclusive); omit for the last level

outcomes.description: outcome_quiz: the outcome types this quiz can result in (required at create time, 1-50 items). Each question choice votes for outcome codes; the outcome with the most votes wins (ties resolved by array order, earlier wins). ai_quiz: optional result tags (0-10; [] removes them) — before writing each report the AI picks one tag per respondent, so leads can be filtered and pushed by it; put the criteria for choosing a tag in its description, and an optional cta shown under that respondent's report. Tags are internal: respondents never see the tag name. Rejected in the knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz scenes.

code.description: Unique outcome code you choose (e.g. "lion"); choices reference it in their outcomes votes. Treat it as a stable identifier — renaming it later breaks references from questions.

name.description: Outcome display name shown on the result page, e.g. "Lion — The Decisive Leader". Plain text.

description.description:
Result-page content shown when this outcome wins. Allows description-scope rich text (headings/lists/links/images etc.). Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

cta.description: Optional CTA button shown on the result page when this outcome wins (e.g. "Book a consultation"). Providing it enables the button.

newWindow.description: Deprecated and ignored: the CTA link always opens in a new window.

redirectUrl.description: outcome_quiz only: http(s) link respondents are sent to right after submitting when this outcome wins, instead of seeing the result page. Only takes effect while redirects are switched on (update_form_settings resultRedirect, Pro). In update_form, omit it to keep the outcome's current link; pass "" or null to remove it. Rejected on ai_quiz result tags.

aiReport.description: ai_quiz scene only (rejected elsewhere): how the AI writes each respondent's report. Sub-keys are merged — pass only the one you change; null or "" clears it.

instructions.description: Generation instructions: what the report should cover, how to read the answers, what to recommend. Plain text (one paragraph per line) or description-scope rich text HTML. Reference a question as {{code}} (visible input questions only; call get_form for the codes) — the AI is pointed at that answer, the answer text itself is not inlined. Unknown codes are rejected. At most 20000 visible characters. get_form returns it in this same {{code}} form.

style.description: Optional style and rules (tone, length, things to avoid), plain text, at most 5000 characters.

length.description: Report length: brief (about 150 words, verdict + 1-2 findings + next steps), standard (default, about 300 words, 2-4 sections, one chart) or detailed (about 650 words, up to 6 sections and 3 charts). null restores standard. brief and standard are hard caps: a longer word count, more sections or more detail asked for in instructions or style is ignored. Only detailed lets a length rule written in style take precedence.

sectionOrder.description: Any scene: the order of the movable result-page sections — dimension (dimension breakdown / radar), booking (the Cal.com booking block), feedback (the feedback block). The overall score / outcome always stays on top and the answer review / share area at the bottom. Keys you leave out keep their default relative order after the ones you list; [] restores the default (booking, dimension, feedback).

levelOrder.description: knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz only: display order of the score levels — asc (default, lowest level first) or desc (highest level first). Applies to the overall levels and every dimension's levels, in the editor and on the result page's level scale. Display only: levels are still stored and matched by minScore ascending, so pass report.levels in ascending order either way. null restores asc.

scoreStyle.description: knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz only: how the result page's overall score card shows the result — scale (a level bar with a marker), ring (a progress ring with the score inside), gauge (a semicircle gauge split by level with a needle) or steps (one bar per level, taller for higher levels). Display only. null (the default) follows the personalized theme: the applied library design's style, or scale when none is applied. Styles that need data the quiz lacks (e.g. steps without levels) fall back to scale.

language.description: Change the form's language. Only allowed while the form has no translation links and is not referenced by other language versions; otherwise rejected.

systemText.description: Answer-page system text overrides as a key→text map. Replaces the whole map (pass {} to clear); empty values are dropped and fall back to the language default.

tools.name: delete_form
tools.description: Move a form into the trash (soft delete) in the current team. The form is hidden from list_forms but kept recoverable for 5 days (then auto-purged); use restore_form to bring it back. Any member of the team can do this. Submission records are kept until permanent purge.

formId.description: The form UUID to move to trash

tools.name: restore_form
tools.description: Restore a form from the trash in the current team (undo delete_form). Any member of the team can restore; errors if the form is not in the trash.

formId.description: The form UUID to restore from trash

tools.name: duplicate_form
tools.description: Duplicate a form in the current team: clones its structure, scoring, report, visual settings and all language translations into a brand-new form owned by you (with fresh share links). Does NOT copy submission records, sharing, integrations, or ban state. Useful for cloning a proven quiz and tweaking it. Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

newTitle.description: Optional title for the copy; defaults to "<source title> (copy)"

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List active templates in the public template library (id, title, scene, use cases, description, category, recommended flag, usage count), most-used first. Filter by useCase to find templates for a goal across scenes (e.g. "personality" also returns scored_quiz personality tests). Use this to find a template, then call create_form_from_template with its id to create a form from it — the fastest way to build a quiz when a suitable template exists.

useCase.description: Filter by use case (what the quiz is for), across scenes, optional: personality / recommendation (product or course finder) / assessment / level_test / trivia / ai_report

isRecommended.description: When true, only return recommended templates

tools.name: create_form_from_template
tools.description: Create a new form in the current team from a public template (find template ids with list_templates). Clones the template structure, scoring/report configuration, visual settings, and all language versions in one call. Links set by the template author are not copied: redirect-after-submit is dropped and result-page CTA buttons keep their text but come over switched off with no URL — tell the user to add their own link and turn them back on. Pass title to override the template title. After creation you can adjust it with update_form / update_question etc. This is the fastest way to build a quiz when a suitable template exists — prefer it over building from scratch with create_form. Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

templateId.description: The template ID to create the form from

title.description: Optional new form title; defaults to the template title

tools.name: add_question
tools.description: Append an item to the end of a form: a question, a page break (Breaker — only formId + type are needed, other fields are ignored) or a display block (Statement / Swiper). Item fields, their per-type / per-scene rules and the question types themselves are exactly those of create_form questions[] — read the full field descriptions there. Limit: a quiz holds at most 50 questions on every plan (page breaks, statements and carousels do not count). An ai_quiz holds at most 20. Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

inputSchema.description: Item fields, their per-type / per-scene rules and the question types themselves are exactly those of create_form questions[] — read the full field descriptions there.

formId.description: The form ID to append the item to

type.description: Question type; Breaker means a page break, no name/choices etc. needed; Statement / Swiper are display-only blocks that collect no answer

code.description: Same as create_form questions[].code.

description.description: Same as create_form questions[].description.

tools.name: insert_question
tools.description: Insert an item at a specific position: a question, a page break (Breaker) or a display block (Statement with `content` / Swiper with `items`). Use after / before to reference an existing field code (from get_form's field.code). To insert at the very front: before references the first field's code. To insert at the end, use add_question. Item fields, their per-type / per-scene rules and the question types themselves are exactly those of create_form questions[] — read the full field descriptions there. Limit: a quiz holds at most 50 questions on every plan (page breaks, statements and carousels do not count). An ai_quiz holds at most 20. Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

inputSchema.description: Item fields, their per-type / per-scene rules and the question types themselves are exactly those of create_form questions[] — read the full field descriptions there.

formId.description: The form ID to insert the item into

after.description: Insert after this code; choose either after or before

before.description: Insert before this code; choose either after or before

type.description: Question type; Breaker means a page break, no name/choices etc. needed; Statement / Swiper are display-only blocks that collect no answer

code.description: Same as create_form questions[].code.

description.description: Same as create_form questions[].description.

tools.name: move_question
tools.description: Move an existing item (question, page break or display block) to a specific position by code. Choose either after or before, referencing another field's code. Move to the front: before references the current first field's code. Move to the end: after references the current last field's code.

code.description: The field code to move (a question, a Breaker or a display block)

after.description: Move after this code; choose either after or before

before.description: Move before this code; choose either after or before

tools.name: update_question
tools.description: Update a single question of an existing form, located by code. Changeable: name / description / explain / required / score / correctAnswer / aiMatch (FillBlank AI grading) / min / max / unit / decimalPlaces (NumberField) / words (Rate scale labels) / maxFiles (Attachment) / choices (replaces ALL choices of a choice-based question). NOT changeable — delete_question then add_question instead: question type, Rate steps, DropDown multiple, Ordering shuffle, Attachment kind. Rate rejects score / correctAnswer / aiMatch. The scored_quiz, outcome_quiz and ai_quiz scenes reject the top-level score / correctAnswer / aiMatch as well: pass choices carrying choices[i].score or choices[i].outcomes instead (TrueFalse outcome votes still need delete + recreate). Display blocks are edited here too, with their own keys: Statement takes content, Swiper takes items (replacing all slides), and both take name / description — every question key is rejected on them.

formId.description: The form ID the question belongs to

code.description: Question code (field.code), from the get_form / create_form return value

description.description:
New question note; pass an empty string to clear. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

explain.description:
New answer explanation (the question's "answer explanation" field, not the question note); pass an empty string to clear. Same rich-text rules as description. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading".

content.description:
Statement block only: the new body text, which is the whole block. Same rich-text rules as description. It cannot be emptied — delete_question the block if you no longer want it. Write HTML, never Markdown: bold not **bold**,
  • not "- item",

    not "## heading". This field also accepts an inline image: put an in it, where src is a direct image URL that renders in (a page URL that merely contains an image does not work). Use finalize_image_upload to host an image yourself, or a direct URL the user supplied. Never invent an image URL — omit the image instead of risking a broken one.

image.description: The slide image: a media ID returned by finalize_image_upload, or the media URL of an image already in this team library. Required — the answer page renders the images and nothing else.

title.description: Optional slide label. Shown in the web editor only (the answer page renders the image), and translatable per language.

description.description: Optional slide note. Web editor only, same as title.

items.description: Swiper block only: replace ALL slides with this list (1-10). Slides get fresh ids, so any translated slide titles / notes for this block have to be rewritten afterwards.

trueLabel.description: TrueFalse only: new custom display text for the "true" option; pass an empty string to clear and fall back to the localized default. Ignored for other question types.

falseLabel.description: TrueFalse only: new custom display text for the "false" option; pass an empty string to clear and fall back to the localized default. Ignored for other question types.

min.description: NumberField only: new minimum allowed value; pass null to remove the lower bound. Ignored for other question types.

max.description: NumberField only: new maximum allowed value; pass null to remove the upper bound. Ignored for other question types.

unit.description: NumberField only: new display unit suffix (e.g. "kg"); pass null or an empty string to clear. Ignored for other question types.

decimalPlaces.description: NumberField only: new number of decimal places allowed (0 = integers only); pass null to reset to the default 0. Ignored for other question types.

words.description: Rate only: new scale labels shown under the rating control (up to 5); pass null or [] to remove the labels. Ignored for other question types.

rateStyle.description: Rate only: new look of the rating control — "star" or "number" (numbered circles); pass null to reset to the default star. Display only, collected ratings are unaffected. Ignored for other question types.

maxFiles.description: Attachment only: how many files a respondent may upload (1-3); pass null to reset to the default 3. Rejected for other question types.

code.description: Optional stable identifier for this choice (option code). Omit to auto-generate. Same identifier rules as the question code; must be unique among the choices of this question. correctAnswer may reference a choice by its label or its code.

score.description: Used only in the scored_quiz scene; the score added when this choice is selected (generates partialScoring). Ignored in the knowledge_quiz scene; rejected in the outcome_quiz scene.

code.description: Outcome code from report.outcomes

weight.description: Votes this pick casts for the outcome; omit for 1. Decimals allowed, 0 = counts for nothing.

outcomes.description: Outcome scene only, and required there on every choice: the outcomes this choice votes for when selected (each code must exist in report.outcomes; a choice may vote for multiple outcomes). Use [] for a neutral choice that votes for nothing. Rejected in the knowledge_quiz / scored_quiz scenes. Each item is an outcome code (one vote) or { code, weight } to make this pick count more or less — e.g. { "code": "lion", "weight": 2 } for a question that should decide the result more than the others. The outcome with the most total votes wins.

dimensionScores.description: scored_quiz scene only: the points this choice adds to each dimension when selected, as a map of dimension code → score, e.g. { "dim_d": 3, "dim_i": 1 }. Each entry overrides this choice's score for that one dimension; a dimension not listed falls back to the plain choice `score`, and an explicit 0 really counts 0. Dimension scores still come only from each dimension's required formula: inside it `{{q}}` is the sum of the selected choices' override-or-score for that dimension, and a question the formula does not reference adds nothing. Codes must exist in report.dimensionAnalysis.dimensions — give dimensions[].code and reference them in the same create_form call. `score` remains the overall score (summed by default, or fed to report.formula when set). Rejected in the knowledge_quiz / outcome_quiz scenes.

choices.description: Replace ALL choices of a choice-based question (SingleCheck / MultiCheck / DropDown / Ordering; rejected for other types). To keep an existing choice's identity (so past answers still match it) pass its current code from get_form; entries without a code get a new auto-generated code. knowledge_quiz scene: if the existing correctAnswer references a code missing from the new choices, pass a new correctAnswer in the same call. scored_quiz scene: set choices[i].score to rebuild Option Scoring (required if the question currently has Option Scoring). outcome_quiz scene: every choice must carry an outcomes vote list (use [] for a neutral choice).

score.description: Score for this question; 0 or omitted + no correctAnswer means not scored

anyOf.description: SingleCheck / single-select DropDown: one choice label or code. FillBlank: the standard answer text.
MultiCheck / multi-select DropDown (multiple=true): the label or code of every correct choice. Ordering: ALL choice labels/codes in the correct order (order-sensitive).
NumberField: a finite number, matched exactly.

correctAnswer.description: New correct answer; the shape follows the question type — see the anyOf branches. Choices are referenced by label or code (use the code when the same label repeats), and they must exist in the question's current choices, or in the `choices` replacement passed in this same call. NumberField answers must stay typeable within min / max and decimalPlaces. Rejected for Rate, and in the scored_quiz / outcome_quiz scenes.

accuracy.description: Accuracy threshold (0-100) at or above which the full score is awarded. Default 80.

extraLevels.description: Optional partial-credit tiers for answers below the full-score threshold, matched from the highest accuracy down.

aiMatch.description: FillBlank AI grading config (knowledge_quiz scene only). Pass an object to enable AI matching (requires the question to have correctAnswer + score > 0); pass null to turn it off and revert to exact-match grading. Omit to leave the existing grading mode untouched.

tools.name: delete_question
tools.description: Delete a single item from a form by code — a question, a page break (Breaker) or a display block (Statement / Swiper). Deleting the last one is allowed (a form can be an empty shell). In the ai_quiz scene, {{code}} references to the deleted question are also removed from report.aiReport.instructions.

formId.description: The form ID the question belongs to

code.description: The code of the question to delete

tools.name: set_dimension_analysis
tools.description: Set the multi-dimension analysis (form.report.dimensionAnalysis) of a form, replacing the dimension list without touching overallAnalysis (title / radar settings you omit are kept). Dimension codes are stable: pass dimensions[].code to keep or set one, or omit it and a dimension with the same name keeps its existing code. Only scored_quiz forms have dimensions; every dimension needs a formula over question codes (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}`), where a question's choices[i].dimensionScores override its plain choice score for that dimension. A dimension still referenced by a question's dimensionScores or by report.formula (the overall formula) cannot be removed. Pass an empty dimensions array to clear the multi-dimension analysis. Call get_form first to read the question and dimension codes. Not supported for knowledge_quiz / outcome_quiz / ai_quiz forms.

title.description: Multi-dimension analysis title

showRadarChart.description: Whether to show the radar chart, default true

When omitted it defaults to the attainable maximum: the formula evaluated with every referenced question at its highest score for this dimension (choices[i].dimensionScores override, else the choice score); 0 when that cannot be estimated, e.g. the formula uses NumberField / date questions.

formula.description: Required: the dimension score formula, usually the sum of the questions in this dimension. Question codes must be wrapped in `{{code}}` (e.g. `{{q1}} + {{q2}}` when you set custom question codes, or `{{__field_abc}} + {{__field_def}}` for auto-generated ones); bare codes are rejected. Inside a dimension formula `{{q}}` is the question's score for THIS dimension: its choices[i].dimensionScores override when set, otherwise the plain choice score. A dimension formula cannot reference other dimensions (only report.formula can). Supported operators: + - * / ( ).

tools.name: prepare_image_upload
tools.description: Step 1 of 2 for adding an image (PNG / JPEG / GIF / WebP) to the current team media library. This tool does NOT receive image bytes — it returns a short-lived presigned URL you upload the file to directly, so even large images never pass through this conversation. Workflow: (1) save the image to a local temp file; (2) if the file is larger than 5MB, compress / downscale it to 5MB or less FIRST (e.g. `sips -Z 2048 in.png --out out.jpg` on macOS, or `magick in.png -resize "2048x2048>" -quality 82 out.webp`) — uploads over 5MB are rejected; (3) call this tool with filename, mimeType and (optionally) fileSize; (4) HTTP PUT the temp file to the returned uploadUrl with the matching Content-Type header, e.g. `curl -X PUT --upload-file <file> "<uploadUrl>" -H "Content-Type: image/png"`; (5) call finalize_image_upload with the returned key; (6) delete the temp file. Max 5MB after compression. Only image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif and image/webp are accepted.

filename.description: Original filename for admin display / download, e.g. "cover.png".

mimeType.description: Image MIME type. Must be one of image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp.

fileSize.description: Optional file size in bytes (of the file you will actually upload, after any compression). If provided it is checked against the 5MB cap and the team storage quota up front; the authoritative check still runs in finalize_image_upload against the actual uploaded size.

tools.name: finalize_image_upload
tools.description: Step 2 of 2 for adding an image: call this AFTER you have PUT the file to the uploadUrl returned by prepare_image_upload. It verifies the uploaded object in storage, records it in the team media library and returns a media id + public URL. To use the image as a quiz cover or a landing-page cover, call update_form with flagImg or landingImage set to the returned media id.

key.description: The object key returned by prepare_image_upload.

filename.description: Original filename for admin display / download (same value passed to prepare_image_upload).

mimeType.description: Image MIME type used at prepare time. Must be one of image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp.

alt.description: Optional alt text for the image.

tools.description: Read submission statistics for a form in the current team: KPI overview (total / today / last 7 / last 30, unique examinees, anonymous, report status counts, average score, latest submission), daily submission trend, channels (by utm_source), UTM combos, login types (anonymous vs registered), device breakdown, and per-question answer distributions. `days` only sets the length of the daily trend; every other block counts all submissions ever made. Answer distributions cover only the first 10 SingleCheck / DropDown / Rate / TrueFalse questions in form order (other types, MultiCheck included, are not counted); each bucket carries the choice label next to its stored value. Use this to gauge how a quiz is performing and to suggest improvements.

Use this to find where respondents drop and improve conversion.

days.description: Look-back window in days, default 30, max 180

tools.name: list_records

Optionally filter by form, report status, and submitted-at range. Reference a respondent by examineeId, never by a masked email; email addresses and phone numbers written into the answers come back masked too. Use get_record for one record's full detail.

status.description: Filter by report generation status, optional. awaiting_gate: the form gates the report behind a respondent verification step and the respondent has not passed it yet, so the AI report has not been generated.

until.description: Only records submitted on/before this ISO datetime, optional

tools.name: get_record

Answers are returned as the respondent wrote them, except that any email address or phone number inside them comes back masked.

tools.name: invite_member
tools.description: Invite someone to the active team (tenant) by email. The pending membership is created immediately and an invitation email with a join link is queued for delivery; the link and its token are never returned in the tool result. Only the team owner or an admin can invite; the call is rejected for other roles. role defaults to "member" and may be "admin". Members can create and edit every form, response, respondent and lead of the team; admins also manage members and team settings. You cannot invite someone as the owner. Fails if the email is already a member or already has a pending invite, or if the team has hit its member limit. Operates on the team this token currently targets — use list_my_tenants / switch_active_tenant to change teams first.

email.description: Email address of the person to invite.

role.description: Role to grant. Defaults to "member"; "admin" also manages members and team settings. Cannot be "owner".

tools.name: list_leads

Newest activity first by default. Filter by status / assignee / tags / created-at range / keyword / whether they have an upcoming booking. Status codes and tag codes are team-defined — call list_lead_settings first to get the valid ones, never guess. Reference a lead by its leadId and a respondent by examineeId, never by a masked email.

status.description: Filter by follow-up status code (see list_lead_settings), optional

assigneeId.description: Filter by the assigned member userId (see list_lead_settings.assignableMembers). Pass "me" for the current token's own user. Optional.

tagCodes.description: Filter by colour tag codes; a lead matches if it has ANY of them (OR). Optional.

keyword.description: Fuzzy match on the respondent's name or email. Matching runs server-side against the real values, so you can search by a full or partial email even though results come back masked.

createdTo.description: Only leads created strictly before this ISO datetime (half-open), optional

tools.name: get_lead
tools.description: View one lead of the current team by leadId: follow-up status, assignee, colour tags, the respondent block, and the next upcoming booking. Optionally include the respondent's submission history (which quizzes they took, with score / level), the team's internal follow-up comments, and the change timeline (status / assignee / tag changes plus submissions). Reference a lead by its leadId and a respondent by examineeId, never by a masked email.

leadId.description: The lead id (the leadId returned by list_leads)

includeComments.description: Include the internal follow-up comments written by team members (default false)

includeActivities.description: Include the change timeline: status / assignee / tag changes and submissions (default false)

tools.name: list_lead_settings

Call this before update_lead / set_lead_tags / assign_leads — status codes, tag codes and member ids are all team-specific and the write tools reject unknown values.

tools.name: update_lead
tools.description: Move one lead of the current team to another follow-up status (e.g. new → contacted). The change is recorded on the lead's timeline. Status codes and tag codes are team-defined — call list_lead_settings first to get the valid ones, never guess.

tools.name: assign_leads
tools.description: Assign one or more leads of the current team to a member, or clear the assignee. Pass every lead id in a single call (up to 50) — do not loop one call per lead. The assignee must be an active member (see list_lead_settings.assignableMembers); pass "me" for yourself, or omit / null to unassign. Each actual change is recorded on the lead's timeline. When assigning, the assignee gets one aggregated in-app notification and, if enabled in their notification preferences, one email for the whole batch; assigning the same owner again does not notify them again.

leadIds.description: The lead ids to assign, max 50 per call

assigneeId.description: The member userId to assign to, or "me" for the current token's own user. Omit (or pass null) to clear the assignee.

tools.name: set_lead_tags
tools.description: Set the colour tags on one or more leads of the current team. Pass every lead id in a single call (up to 50) — do not loop. mode: "replace" (default, overwrite the whole tag set — for editing a single lead), "add" or "remove" (for batches, where each lead has different tags and overwriting would wipe other people's tags). Tag codes must exist in the team's tag library (see list_lead_settings.tags); "remove" also accepts stale codes. Changes are recorded on each lead's timeline.

leadIds.description: The lead ids to tag, max 50 per call

tags.description: The tag codes to apply, from list_lead_settings.tags[].code

Not idempotent: if the call times out it may still have succeeded, so retrying blindly can create a duplicate — check first, then retry only if it is really missing.

Pass utmSource to get every link and snippet tagged for one channel. Use this to answer "give me the link / the embed code" and to sanity-check a launch; change the switches with update_form_settings.

utmSource.description: Optional channel tag applied to the links and snippets (letters, digits, _ and - only, max 64). Omitted or invalid = no tag, in which case the embed script forwards whatever utm_* the host page already has.
